title: FDA highly variable drug: which analysis applies, by estimated sWR
subject: method selection

rule.statement: Estimate the within-reference standard deviation sWR from the replicate design. If sWR is less than 0.294, analyse by conventional average bioequivalence. If sWR is 0.294 or greater, apply reference-scaled average bioequivalence together with the point-estimate constraint of 80.00-125.00%.
rule.applies_to: the ESTIMATED sWR from the study, not an assumed population CV

expected.why: above sqrt(ln(1+0.30^2)) = 0.293560 and still below 0.294 - the interval where a derived threshold and the guidance figure disagree
the boundary itself; the criterion is >=, so it scales

refuses.why: a standard deviation cannot be negative; refuse rather than route

separate_and_not_this_rule.note: Within-subject %CV of 30% or greater is how a drug is CLASSIFIED as highly variable. It is a different question from which analysis applies, asked at a different time, of a different quantity. The two numbers are within 0.0005 of each other and must not be merged.

source.verified_by: primary document, read at the cited section
source.limitation: The guidance has now been read. Both III.C and Appendix G state this rule and agree on the boundary: III.C says 'If the estimated within-subject standard deviation of the reference is < 0.294, the average BE two one-sided test procedure should be used ... Otherwise, the reference-scaled average BE procedure should be used', and Appendix G step 1 says 'a. If sWR < 0.294 ... b. If sWR >= 0.294'. This closes tier 1A. It does not touch tier 1B: the document contains no worked dataset - no input values, no published answer - so there is nothing here to reproduce numerically.

a_second_rule_uses_the_same_number.where: section III.A, in vitro permeation testing for topical drug products
a_second_rule_uses_the_same_number.text: the reference-scaled average BE approach is used for the endpoint only if it has a sWR > 0.294. The regular average BE approach ... is used for the endpoint with sWR <= 0.294.
a_second_rule_uses_the_same_number.why_recorded: Same threshold, OPPOSITE treatment of the boundary, different products. A study whose estimated sWR is exactly 0.294 is scaled under Appendix G and unscaled under III.A. Recorded so that fda_hvd_method_for is never reused for an in vitro permeation study - the same scoping lesson the M13A minimums taught, arriving from a third direction.

covers: The decision rule only. This case asserts nothing about the RSABE criterion arithmetic, which is Phase 2A and not implemented.
history: Added as part of a correction. An earlier version of this package derived the switching threshold as cv_to_log_sd(0.30) = 0.293560, marked it DERIVED, and enforced with an AST-level test that 0.294 must never appear in the source. That inverted the relationship between the package and the regulator: 0.294 is FDA's stated criterion, not a rounded presentation of this package's arithmetic. The row at sWR = 0.2937 is the study the earlier version would have misrouted.
